messages.content: We have fall break nailed down now: Friday, October 10 through Tuesday, October 14, four nights. It will be the three of us from Dallas to New Orleans. I want to see whether flying both ways or using an overnight train for one leg makes sense, then compare the Warehouse District with somewhere near City Park. Keep the whole trip under $3,200 if possible.

I’ll compare three structures: nonstop flights both ways, train outbound with a flight home, and flight outbound with the train home. I’ll include the airport or station transfers, baggage, and one room explicitly rated for three guests. Is the $3,200 ceiling for transportation and lodging only, or should it also leave room for museums and local transportation?
Include local transportation and about $350 for admissions and music. Meals can stay outside it. We can use DFW or Love Field.

That leaves roughly $2,850 for intercity transportation, lodging, and local rides. One issue is already apparent: Dallas does not have a direct overnight train to New Orleans. The rail itinerary requires a change in San Antonio and takes about 30 to 34 hours, depending on direction and the operating day. I’m checking whether either direction can fit the fixed Friday-to-Tuesday window without reducing the four New Orleans nights.
I didn’t realize it was that long. Show it anyway, but don’t quietly turn four nights into three.

The outbound rail option would require leaving Dallas Thursday around midday, changing trains overnight in San Antonio, and reaching New Orleans Friday evening. You would still have four hotel nights, but the overall trip would begin a day early. Representative coach pricing is $171 per person, or $513 for three. A private option is much higher: two roomettes are needed because one cannot hold three travelers, and the combined quote is about $1,145 for that leg. Checked baggage is included within Amtrak’s limits, but checked service must be available at both stations. A ride to Dallas Union Station and one from New Orleans Union Passenger Terminal would add about $45 total.
Coach for thirty-plus hours is not realistic, and two roomettes wipe out the reason to consider it. What about train home?

The return is less compatible. It leaves New Orleans Tuesday morning, changes overnight in San Antonio, and reaches Dallas Wednesday afternoon. That preserves four hotel nights but extends the trip beyond Tuesday. Coach is about $498 for three; two roomettes total roughly $1,090. Add about $45 for station rides. Neither train direction stays entirely inside October 10-14, so rail only works if the travel window expands on one end.
Then price the flights. I’d rather make an informed decision than force the train.

The best complete flight comparison is: American nonstop from DFW, departing Friday at 8:05 a.m. and arriving MSY at 9:32 a.m.; return Tuesday at 6:20 p.m., arriving DFW at 8:02 p.m. Regular Main Cabin is $319 per person, $957 total. Each traveler gets a personal item and carry-on; first checked bags are $40 each way, so one shared checked bag would add $80. A Southwest pairing from Love Field leaves at 9:15 a.m. and returns at 5:35 p.m. It is $346 per person, $1,038 total, with two checked bags per person included. Both are nonstop.
Use one checked bag in the American math. What should I allow for getting to and from the airports?

Using hired rides, I’d allow $95 total for home-to-DFW and DFW-to-home, plus $72 for MSY-to-hotel and hotel-to-MSY. That makes American $1,204 including one checked bag and all airport transfers. Southwest comes to about $1,195 if rides to Love Field total about $85 and the New Orleans rides remain $72. Southwest is therefore about $9 less on the complete transport calculation, while American’s times provide slightly more time in New Orleans.
That is close enough that the hotel area matters more. Compare rooms that genuinely work for three. I don’t want a king room described as suitable just because a rollaway might exist.

In the Warehouse District, a representative refundable two-queen room at The Higgins is $1,168.40 for four nights including taxes. The published occupancy is four, so three guests are covered without a rollaway. A second option, a two-queen studio at Residence Inn New Orleans Downtown, is $1,296.12 including taxes; it also lists occupancy of four and includes breakfast. Neither quote requires an extra-person charge for the third guest, but the final checkout page should still show all three names or an occupancy count of three.
And near City Park? We want the sculpture garden and botanical garden, but we also have the World War II Museum, Ogden, and one music night.

The closest credible three-person comparison is a two-queen room in the Mid-City/Canal Street area, about a mile and a half from City Park, at $1,084.76 including taxes. It is rated for four guests. Inventory immediately beside the park is mostly small inns with one-bed rooms or vacation rentals whose fees narrow the price advantage. From the Mid-City option, allow about $18 round trip to City Park, $36 round trip to the Warehouse District museums, and $30 round trip for the music evening. Streetcar use could lower that, but three riders and transfers make hired rides more efficient for some legs.
Put both areas into full-trip totals. Use Southwest for now, the $350 activity amount, and enough local transportation that we are not pretending every trip will go perfectly.

With Southwest, the Warehouse District plan is approximately $2,823.40: $1,038 flights, $157 airport rides, $1,168.40 at The Higgins, $110 for local rides and transit, and $350 for admissions and music. That leaves $376.60 below the $3,200 ceiling. The Mid-City plan is approximately $2,749.76: the same $1,038 flights, $157 airport rides, $1,084.76 lodging, $120 for local rides and transit, and $350 for activities. It leaves $450.24. Both fit, and both include a modest transportation cushion.
I expected City Park to win by more. Is the Warehouse District actually better for the itinerary?

For this mix, yes. The Warehouse District puts the World War II Museum and Ogden Museum within a short walk, and it shortens the trip to the likely music areas. City Park becomes one planned half-day ride rather than the anchor for every day. Mid-City saves $83.64 on the room, but some of that is consumed by repeated rides to the museums and evening venues. The net trip difference is only $73.64.
Can the Residence Inn justify the extra cost for three people, or is it just more room than we need?

It adds $127.72 over The Higgins. The studio gives you more floor space and breakfast for three, which could offset some meal spending, but meals are outside this trip ceiling. For the budget you defined, The Higgins two-queen room is the cleaner comparison: confirmed sleeping surfaces for three, the stronger museum location, and no need to rely on a sofa bed.
Now compare American plus The Higgins against Southwest plus The Higgins one last time. Include the bag and rides exactly as you did before.

American plus The Higgins totals $2,832.40: $957 airfare, $80 for one checked bag, $167 in airport rides, $1,168.40 lodging, $110 local transportation, and $350 activities. Southwest plus The Higgins totals $2,823.40: $1,038 airfare, no checked-bag charge, $157 airport rides, and the same $1,628.40 for hotel, local transportation, and activities. Southwest is $9 cheaper overall; American departs 70 minutes earlier and returns 45 minutes later.
So the train does not fit the fixed dates, both flight plans fit the budget, and Warehouse is only slightly more than Mid-City once rides are counted. Is that the fair conclusion?

Yes. Rail requires either a Thursday departure or a Wednesday return and takes more than 30 hours with a San Antonio transfer, so it does not fit the fixed October 10-14 travel window. Both nonstop flight plans fit the $3,200 ceiling with The Higgins: Southwest at about $2,823.40 and American at about $2,832.40. Mid-City is cheapest at about $2,749.76 with Southwest, but the Warehouse District better supports the two museum visits and music night; its City Park outing remains manageable as a single round-trip ride. No reservation has been made. Before purchase, the live checks are the fare rules, the Southwest baggage allowance in effect for these dates, the hotel’s final three-guest occupancy display, and cancellation terms.
